r.정치 구도: It became an Islamic republic after the 1979 Islamic Revolution toppled the monarchy. Voters elect the president and parliament directly, but above them is a supreme leader appointed for life who has the final say on the military, the judiciary and nuclear policy. The clergy-dominated Guardian Council vets election candidates in advance, sometimes disqualifying reformists en masse. The Revolutionary Guards hold a big share not only of military power but of the economy. After a woman died in custody during a hijab crackdown in 2022, nationwide protests followed.

t.why: It sits on the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil and LNG used to pass. It has led an 'axis of resistance' backing Lebanon's Hezbollah, Yemen's Houthis and Iraqi militias, influencing many conflicts in the Middle East. Long at odds with the United States and Israel over its nuclear program, it saw the 2015 nuclear deal falter when the United States withdrew in 2018. War broke out again after their strikes in June 2025 and then February 2026, in which the supreme leader was killed; his son succeeded him in March. Iran effectively closed the strait, and traffic is still far below normal. It is close to Russia and China and a member of BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
t.rel: Long at odds with Israel and the United States, it was at war after their strikes in June 2025 and again in February 2026. It has backed armed groups such as Lebanon's Hezbollah and Yemen's Houthis, and restored relations with Saudi Arabia in 2023.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1962. Iran used to sell crude oil to Korea, but trade stopped after US sanctions, and oil payments frozen in Korean banks became a diplomatic issue. Much of Korea's oil came through the Strait of Hormuz, so since it was blocked Korea has rerouted supplies through other routes and suppliers. The strait directly affects Korean fuel prices. Teheran-ro in Seoul got its name when the two cities became sister cities in 1977.
t.know: Iran's new year begins at the spring equinox, and the new year festival, Nowruz, is a tradition more than 3,000 years old.
etext: Its crude oil reserves are among the world's largest, and its natural gas reserves rank at the very top alongside Russia's. It shares an offshore gas field with Qatar.
US sanctions make it hard to sell oil officially, so it ships it mainly to China at a discount. Meanwhile it has built domestic industries such as petrochemicals, steel, cars and cement.
The currency keeps falling and inflation is very high. Foundations linked to the Revolutionary Guards control a large share of the economy, making private investment difficult.
